content.text: Mizerka is a popular Polish trick-taking game for three players, played with a standard 52-card deck. It is a game of 'Contracts', where each player must eventually choose to play through six distinct game types (four suits, No Trump, and the eponymous 'Mizerka'â€”a misere avoidance contract). It features a unique 'Partial Deal' bidding phase and a talon exchange that allows players to refine their hands. It is highly strategic, requiring players to balance their aggressive and defensive contracts throughout 18 total rounds.
Rooted in the Slavic tradition of trick-taking games like preference and thousand (1000). It became a standardized parlor game in Poland during the 20th century.

Three players. Play is clockwise. Any player may deal first; the turn to deal passes clockwise. In each deal the three roles are: dealer (deals and has a quota of 1 trick in trump contracts, 7 in mizerka), forehand or left of dealer (chooses the contract after seeing six cards and has quota 7 in trump contracts, 1 in mizerka), and middlehand or right of dealer (quota 5 in both). The player to dealer's left leads to the first trick.
Each player gets 6 cards. 6 for the talon. Then the rest (13 total each + 13 for talon).

items.text: Standard (six contracts): Six contracts: clubs, hearts, spades, diamonds, no trumps, and mizerka (misère). Each player chooses each contract once over 18 deals.
Contract order: Contract is chosen by player to dealer's left after seeing first six cards; no other variant specified in source.
Talon exchange: Left of dealer exchanges first, then right of dealer, then dealer if talon remains; no obligation to discard.
